Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor.ext

Class EditorContext

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.texteditor.ext.EditorContext
public final class EditorContext extends Object
The capability facade the editor hands an extension at
invalid reference 
TextEditorExtension#onEditorStarted
. Every capability is gated on the permissions the user granted: calling a method whose permission was not granted is a silent no-op (and has(TextEditorPermission) reports the truth), so an over-reaching extension degrades gracefully instead of misbehaving.

The delegates are wired by the broker to the live editor panel; in headless tests they are stubs, which keeps this type AWT-free.

      public EditorContext(Set<TextEditorPermission> granted, Consumer<String> showMessage, Runnable openFile, Runnable saveFile)
      Back-compatible form without the output-console capabilities.

      showMessage - writes a line to the editor status line (always allowed)
      openFile - opens a file dialog (gated on TextEditorPermission.FILE_IO)

    • navigateTo

      public void navigateTo(String path, int line)
      Asks the editor to move the caret to the 1-based line of path (go-to-definition / find-occurrences jumps); no-op without TextEditorPermission.READ, since navigating reads the document. The out-of-range line is clamped by the host, not here.

    • getBreakpoints

      public List<Integer> getBreakpoints(String path)
      Returns:
      the 1-based lines carrying a user-toggled breakpoint in path (the gutter's state), ascending; empty without TextEditorPermission.DEBUG or when the host has no breakpoint surface. The debugger installs its requests from this list.

    • publishCompletions

      public void publishCompletions(String path, List<String> candidates)
      Publishes completion candidates for path to the editor's completion strip; an empty list clears it. No-op without TextEditorPermission.READ or when the host has no strip. Presentation only — accepting a candidate is the user's action.
